transcript: With a ceremonial gavel strike, the engine of state political power shifted into drive for the 2023 legislative session. Hello and welcome to the impact. I'm Mike McClanahan. This is a budget year, so lawmakers have a total of 105 days to send a state spending plan to the governor. Approving a new budget is the only task they are required by law to complete before adjourning, but there are a lot of additional priorities for the various political leaders in the House and Senate. Some of the issues you can expect to hear legislators debate include out-of-control housing costs and the increase in homelessness around the state. changes to the law that determines when police are allowed to engage in high-speed pursuits. New gun restrictions, including a license requirement for firearm purchases. The stopgap misdemeanor drug possession statute which replaced the state's old felony drug law is set to expire in July. That means legislators will also be debating whether to move towards stronger penalties for drug possession or further towards decriminalization. Democrats come into 2023 with larger majorities in the House and Senate. Democratic budget leaders say they are focused on addressing the shortage of workers in critical fields and finding ways to support renters, people facing foreclosure, and would-be home buyers who have been priced out of the market. Across the aisle, Republican leaders say responding to crime and removing regulatory hurdles to new home construction are among their top priorities this year. reducing homelessness and increasing the supply of housing are also at the top of Democratic Governor Jay Inslee's 2023 legislative agenda. He is proposing a $4 billion referendum that would allow the state to issue bonds outside its debt limit with the goal of building more than 20,000 new housing units over the next 10 years. The governor's legislative agenda also calls for a new approach to salmon recovery and for funding to explore alternative power sources that could equal the output of the Snake River dams. We discussed these topics and more during a one-on-one interview Monday, just as the session was getting underway. It's 2023. You've got an ambitious legislative agenda. If you could give us sort of the highlights of that in a bullet point fashion, please do.
